item.stem:

item.figure_description:
A map enclosed in a wavy rectangular border, labeled "Map drawn to scale" in the bottom-left corner. Five locations are marked with solid black dots and labels:
- "Ourtown" is located in the lower-middle portion of the map.
- "Acton" is northwest of Ourtown, connected to Ourtown by a straight path line.
- "Burley" is directly north of Acton, connected to Acton by a vertical straight path line.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
On the map, 1 cm represents 10 km on the land.

[Image: Map showing towns and roads]

On the land, about how far apart are the towns Melville and Folley?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangular map showing three towns marked with dots: Melville near the top center, Mockem on the middle left, and Folley to the lower right. A thick curved black line representing "Red River" runs diagonally across the map from the lower-left to the upper-right. Thin lines represent roads: one goes vertically down through Melville and Mockem, and another connects Melville curving down and to the right, crossing the Red River and passing through Folley. In the bottom right corner of the map, an inset box contains a scale line segment marked with vertical end-ticks labeled "1 cm = 10 km". On the map, the straight-line distance between Melville and Folley is approximately 5 times the length of the 1 cm scale bar.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Four students watched the traffic passing their school for 1 hour.

The table shows what they saw:

| Type of Vehicle | Number |
| :--- | :---: |
| Cars | 60 |
| Bicycles | 30 |
| Buses | 10 |
| Trucks | 20 |

Each student drew a graph to show the results. Which graph shows the results correctly?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four graphical representations of the traffic data:
- Option A: A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The bars correspond to: Cars = 60 (solid black bar), Bicycles = 30 (light gray bar), Buses = 10 (medium gray bar), Trucks = 20 (white bar with black border).
- Option B: A pictograph with a legend stating '1 wheel = 10 vehicles'. Cars has 5 wheels, Bicycles has 4 wheels, Buses has 1 wheel, and Trucks has 2 wheels.
- Option C: A vertical bar graph with the same axis and colors as Option A, showing: Cars = 60, Bicycles = 30, Buses = 20, Trucks = 10.
- Option D: A pie chart divided into four sectors: Cars covers the right half (180°, solid black). Bicycles covers the bottom-left quadrant (90°, light gray). The remaining top-left quadrant is divided between Buses (a larger sector, medium gray) and Trucks (a smaller sector, white).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
